document: LUCI Field Activation Guide — client version
purpose: Tailored step-by-step instructions to replace the generic 'Try it' callouts in the client FAG. Inline in the doc, no portal links.
methodology: Drafted from Mike's demo/training transcripts (Ameristar 2026-06-16, Angel of the Wind 2026-04-23) plus the functional activation guide copy doc. Every step is a DRAFT pending review by Mike Epstein or a LUCI FDE against the live product before it ships.

reviewRequired: Mike Epstein or a LUCI FDE must verify each workflow against the live product before it is published in the client FAG.
pipelineNote: Content (custom messages, promos, event graphics) lives in the CMS (Telemetry TV) and reaches LUCI as a channel: Telemetry player HDMI out → LUCI IP encoder → source in LUCI's list. That CMS→encoder→LUCI path is the same one-time setup behind most Marketing use cases, so it's written once here and referenced.

useCases.title: Push a message to every screen in under two minutes.
useCases.prerequisites: Your message exists as an image or short video, and a Telemetry player is already wired into a LUCI encoder so its content shows up as a channel in LUCI. If not, do the one-time Setup first.
setup: In Telemetry TV, open Media and drag your message asset in (or pull it from a linked OneDrive/Canva). Set a validity end-date if the message is temporary so it auto-removes.
Create a Playlist, add the message to it, and assign the playlist to a Telemetry player. That player's output feeds a LUCI IP encoder, so the message now appears as a channel in LUCI's source list.
steps: Open LUCI in your browser from any device and log in.
On the property map, zoom out until every display on the floor is in view.
Use the lasso tool to select every TV on the property — or select just the zones you want to reach.
In the source list, pick the channel carrying your message. Every selected display flips to it immediately, live, with no ticket or call.
To drop back: set a revert time (e.g., 60 seconds) and the floor returns to its scheduled content on its own — or apply your 'normal' preset when you're done.
useCases.revert: Set a revert time in seconds on the push, or apply a return-to-normal preset. The floor drops back to scheduled content automatically.
assumptions: Lasso-then-select-source is the fastest path for a whole-property push (vs. building a preset). Confirm with Mike.
Revert time can be set on an ad-hoc push, not only on a scheduled preset. Confirm.
If the message must land on EVERY screen including the marquee/outdoor, those displays must be on the map (connected via encoder). Confirm scope.

useCases.title: Daypart your restaurant promotions to catch guests at the decision point.
useCases.prerequisites: Your dining spot asset exists and a Telemetry player → LUCI encoder channel is set up for it (see UC1 Setup).
setup: Same one-time CMS setup as UC1: load the dining spot in Telemetry TV, put it on a playlist, assign to a player so it appears as a channel in LUCI.
steps: In LUCI, open Presets and create a new preset (e.g., 'Pre-lunch dining spot').
Add the displays you want to reach — the floor-wide set, not just the screens near the restaurants. Select them on the map or from the venue list.
For each display in the preset, set its target to the dining spot channel.
Save the preset.
Open the Event Scheduler. Add the preset to the calendar at 11:00am (and a second entry at 5:00pm for dinner). Set it to repeat daily, or pick specific days.
Set a revert time on each entry (e.g., 60 minutes) so the floor drops back to regular rotation automatically — or schedule a 'normal' preset to follow it.
useCases.revert: Revert time on the preset, or a following 'normal' preset on the calendar.
assumptions: A single preset can target a floor-wide display set (vs. needing one per venue). Confirm.
Revert time is set per scheduled event. Confirm where the revert field lives — on the preset or on the scheduled event.

useCases.title: Run customized content by zone — indoor and outdoor — from one control panel.
useCases.prerequisites: Each zone's content is loaded in Telemetry TV and each is on its own player → LUCI encoder channel (one source per zone's content). Confirm with your A/V team which external displays (marquee, outdoor signs) are currently connected through LUCI — they only appear on the map if they're on an encoder.
setup: In Telemetry TV, load each zone's content as a separate playlist on a separate player (one player per simultaneously-running piece of content). Each player → LUCI encoder → its own channel in LUCI's source list.
For outdoor signage: confirm the marquee/outdoor displays are wired into LUCI encoders. If they are, they show up as displays on the map and are managed exactly like indoor screens.
steps: In LUCI, open the property map and pick the first zone (e.g., sports book). Select it from the venue list or tap its tag.
Select the displays in that zone, then in the source list pick that zone's content channel. They flip immediately.
Repeat for each zone — main floor, bar, lobby, marquee — each running its own content at the same time.

To make it repeat: build one preset per zone (displays + that zone's channel) and schedule each on its own calendar. Zone schedules are independent, so the sports book can run on one cadence while the bar runs on another.
Walk the floor to confirm each zone is playing what you intended, and adjust the channel or schedule from the same panel.
useCases.revert: Each zone can be returned to its standing content by applying that zone's 'normal' preset, or by scheduling it.
assumptions: Each simultaneously-running content stream needs its own player/encoder channel. Confirm the player count recommendation with Mike.
External signage is IP-controllable through a LUCI encoder. Confirm the marquee specifically — it may need a separate integration.
A preset can be scoped to a single venue/zone. Confirm.

useCases.title: Build an event campaign that escalates automatically.
useCases.prerequisites: Your event promo asset(s) are loaded in Telemetry TV and on a player → LUCI encoder channel (see UC1 Setup). Confirm whether 'escalation' is a single feature or a preset sequence (see assumptions).
setup: In Telemetry TV, load the event promo asset(s). For higher frequency closer to the event, build a playlist that rotates the promo more often (or a shorter spot list) — frequency is controlled on the CMS side, zone coverage on the LUCI side.
steps: In LUCI, build a series of presets, each wider than the last: Preset A = one zone (e.g., lobby) on the event channel; Preset B = lobby + concourse; Preset C = full floor on the event channel.
Open the Event Scheduler and place Preset A on the calendar for two weeks out, Preset B for one week out, and Preset C for the week of the event. Each can repeat daily during its window.
To fill slow dayparts between campaign windows, schedule a separate preset that pushes loyalty and dining offers during historically slow windows.
Schedule a 'return to baseline' preset for the day after the event (or set revert times on Preset C) so no stale event content keeps running.
Build it once — the calendar ramps and resets on its own from there.
useCases.revert: A scheduled 'return to baseline' preset the day after the event, plus revert times on the campaign presets, returns the whole floor to normal automatically.
assumptions: Escalation is built as a SEQUENCE of presets on the calendar, not a single 'escalating' feature. Confirm with Mike — LUCI may have a newer campaign/escalation tool not covered in the transcripts.
Frequency (how often the spot plays) is controlled in the CMS playlist, not in LUCI. Confirm.
Zone coverage is controlled in the LUCI preset. Confirm.

useCases.title: Set your floor's audio to match the room's energy, all day.
Make every jackpot a floor event, automatically.
Reconfigure the entire property in seconds.
Direct guest attention to a new game area from the moment it opens.
Build the whole property's schedule in one session, then let it run.
Resolve service requests from wherever you are — including after hours.
Find problems before guests do.
useCases.prerequisites: LUCI open on the property map. (Live today: per-display online/offline status. The fuller health dashboard and alerting ship in the upcoming release.)
steps: Open LUCI and go to the property map.
Each display shows its status in real time — green means it's on and communicating, red means it's off or not responding.
Scan the map (or a single venue) for any red/offline displays — LUCI knows the moment a TV drops off the network.
Tap an offline display to see its name and start narrowing the cause: a power issue, a network issue, or both.
To get it fixed without a phone call: route the offline status to your ticketing system so the right person is dispatched — or note it and schedule the fix for a quiet window.
Walk in already knowing what needs attention, instead of hearing about it from a guest at the bar.
assumptions: The red/green online/offline indicator is live in the current build (Mike demoed it). Confirm.

Auto-routing offline status to a ticketing system is an integration — Mike phrased it as a capability ('we could take this information and send it to your system to generate a ticket'). Confirm whether it's wired today or part of the upcoming release.
Confirm whether audio-zone and lighting endpoints show the same online/offline indicator, or only video displays.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — reframed around live offline detection (Ameristar); confirm ticketing-integration status

useCases.title: Configure a private event once, then activate it and let it revert on its own.
Add an endpoint to LUCI — video, audio, or lighting.
useCases.prerequisites: You have an admin PIN and the device's IP address (it must match the field device — the set-top box/TV, the DSP, or the lighting system).
steps: Log in to LUCI with your admin PIN.
Left menu → Administration → Map Modes → Device Setup [Administration].
Select the device type: Video, Audio, or Lighting [Devices]. (On LUCI v2.34.0+, use the Endpoint Manager instead.)
Navigate the map to where the endpoint lives.
Right-click (or long-press) the map → Add Endpoint (for lighting, Add Device).
Video only: pick the Brand from the dropdown. (Audio and lighting skip this.)
Name the endpoint — this is the label shown on the UI.
Notes: add asset tagging or other info you want to track.
Device Address: enter the IP that matches the field device (video: the set-top box/TV; audio: the DSP; lighting: the lighting system).
Assign the endpoint to a Venue so every user on that venue can reach it (unless you restrict it per user — see IT UC03).
Video only: toggle Auto Power to let a watchdog keep the device powered on.
Set any other relevant options, then click Save.
To edit later: right-click the device on the map (or in the Assigned list) → Edit Endpoint.
assumptions: Click-path is the same across video/audio/lighting; only the device-type tab and the IP target differ. Confirm.
v2.34.0+ uses Endpoint Manager — confirm which version the client is on so steps point at the right screen.
Assigning to a Venue gives all venue users access by default; restricting per user is done in User Management → Access (IT UC03). Confirm the linkage.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — from 3 JSM KB articles (video/audio/lighting endpoint add/edit/remove)

useCases.title: Keep every config, backup, and guide for your system in one place.
useCases.prerequisites: Access to the LUCI Smartsheet and support site — ask your FDE if you don't have credentials yet.
steps: For config and backup files: open the LUCI Smartsheet your FDE shared with you — every config file and backup for your system lives there, fully documented.
For user guides, admin guides, and walkthrough videos: open the LUCI support site.
Before you open a ticket: walk the basic troubleshooting guides on the support site — a lot of issues you can clear yourself.
To report an issue or request a change: file it through the support site's ticketing — no phone tag, no waiting on a vendor.
Reference these any time you need to do something yourself without calling your integrator.
assumptions: Mike says 'we share everything through Smartsheet' — confirm every client is provisioned Smartsheet access by default, or whether it's on request.
Confirm the support site URL and how clients get credentials (ask FDE).
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — from Ameristar transcript (Smartsheet + support site); confirm provisioning with FDE

useCases.title: Define who can change what — by role, by zone, by team.
useCases.prerequisites: You have an admin PIN. The KB article covers per-user source permissions (View/Edit). Confirm with Mike whether zone-level and feature-level access (schedules, health checks) live in this same screen or elsewhere.
steps: Log in to LUCI with your admin PIN.
Navigate to User Management → Access.
Select the user whose access you're setting. Do this before touching any controls — permissions are edited per selected user.
Open the Source tab. You'll see every source in the system and this user's current permission for each.
For each source, set the View permission: Enabled (user can tune a display to it), Disabled (visible in the user's list but can't tune to it), or Hidden (not shown to this user at all).
Set the Edit permission per source: On (user can edit that source's details — edits apply to all users) or Off (read-only for this user).
To set the same permission across every source at once, use the batch controls at the top right: the Options dropdown sets View for all sources, and the Edit All toggle sets Edit for all.
For source-by-source control, use the dropdown and toggle next to each source individually.
Repeat for each user. Permissions take effect immediately.
assumptions: KB covers source-level View/Edit per user. The FAG frames access as 'by role, by zone, by team' — confirm with Mike whether role/zone abstractions exist on top of per-user-per-source, or whether that framing is aspirational.
'Edit On applies for all users of the system' per the KB — confirm source-detail edits are global, not per-user.
Confirm whether non-source permissions (who can edit schedules, run health checks, manage presets) are controlled here or in a separate admin area.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — from JSM KB article 139427856; needs Mike to confirm role/zone scope

useCases.title: Set up kiosk mode so any staffer can control their area from a phone or mounted touchscreen.
useCases.prerequisites: A small mounted touchscreen (LUCI's ~large-smartphone-sized panel) or any phone with a browser. The venue/zone and the sources you want that kiosk to reach are already on the map.
steps: In LUCI, create a kiosk user (User Management → Access) and assign it a PIN.
Filter that user's access to the venue or zone the kiosk controls, and to just the sources they should pick from (see IT UC03 for access filtering).
Set the user to kiosk mode — list-based control with no map. They get a simple list of displays and channels, not the property map.
Mount the small touchscreen in the space (conference room, cabana, etc.), or have the staffer open the LUCI URL on their phone.
The user logs in with their PIN and lands on a simple list of their displays and channels — tap a display, pick a channel, done.
For a cabana: the guest uses the mounted touchscreen to choose the channel for that cabana's screen — self-serve, no staff involved.
For a conference room: the touchscreen makes it easy to switch between a projector and a flat screen and change the channel.
useCases.revert: n/a — kiosk users persist until changed.
assumptions: Kiosk mode = list-based control without the map (Mike's three user levels: admin, user, kiosk). Confirm the exact toggle/setting name in the current build.
The small touchscreens are LUCI-provided hardware (~large-smartphone-sized) — confirm whether they're included or a separate purchase.
Per-cabana guest self-serve implies a kiosk user per cabana or a shared 'cabana guest' kiosk — confirm the recommended setup with Will/Mike.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — from 07-14 Cabana/Room/Event Control transcript; confirm kiosk-mode specifics with Will/Mike
